["vlnpe_abs", "Abstract: Recent Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) advancements are promising, but their idealized assumptions about robot movement and control fail to reflect physically embodied deployment challenges. To bridge this gap, we introduce VLN-PE, a physically realistic VLN platform supporting humanoid, quadruped, and wheeled robots. For the first time, we systematically evaluate several ego-centric VLN methods in physical robotic settings across different technical pipelines, including classification models for single-step discrete action prediction, a diffusion model for dense waypoint prediction, and a train-free, map-based large language model (LLM) integrated with path planning. Our results reveal significant performance degradation due to limited robot observation space, environmental lighting variations, and physical challenges like collisions and falls. This also exposes locomotion constraints for legged robots in complex environments. VLN-PE is highly extensible, allowing seamless integration of new scenes beyond MP3D, thereby enabling more comprehensive VLN evaluation. Despite the weak generalization of current models in physical deployment, VLN-PE provides a new pathway for improving cross-embodiment's overall adaptability. We hope our findings and tools inspire the community to rethink VLN limitations and advance robust, practical VLN models. The code is available at this https URL .", [["this https URL", "https://crystalsixone.github.io/vln_pe.github.io/"]]]
["navila_abs", "Abstract: This paper proposes to solve the problem of Vision-and-Language Navigation with legged robots, which not only provides a flexible way for humans to command but also allows the robot to navigate through more challenging and cluttered scenes. However, it is non-trivial to translate human language instructions all the way to low-level leg joint actions. We propose NaVILA, a 2-level framework that unifies a Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) with locomotion skills. Instead of directly predicting low-level actions from VLA, NaVILA first generates mid-level actions with spatial information in the form of language, (e.g., "moving forward 75cm"), which serves as an input for a visual locomotion RL policy for execution. NaVILA substantially improves previous approaches on existing benchmarks. The same advantages are demonstrated in our newly developed benchmarks with IsaacLab, featuring more realistic scenes, low-level controls, and real-world robot experiments. We show more results at this https URL", [["this https URL", "https://navila-bot.github.io/"], ["this https URL", "https://navila-bot.github.io/"]]]
["barkour_abs", "Abstract: Animals have evolved various agile locomotion strategies, such as sprinting, leaping, and jumping. There is a growing interest in developing legged robots that move like their biological counterparts and show various agile skills to navigate complex environments quickly. Despite the interest, the field lacks systematic benchmarks to measure the performance of control policies and hardware in agility. We introduce the Barkour benchmark, an obstacle course to quantify agility for legged robots. Inspired by dog agility competitions, it consists of diverse obstacles and a time based scoring mechanism. This encourages researchers to develop controllers that not only move fast, but do so in a controllable and versatile way. To set strong baselines, we present two methods for tackling the benchmark. In the first approach, we train specialist locomotion skills using on-policy reinforcement learning methods and combine them with a high-level navigation controller. In the second approach, we distill the specialist skills into a Transformer-based generalist locomotion policy, named Locomotion-Transformer, that can handle various terrains and adjust the robot's gait based on the perceived environment and robot states. Using a custom-built quadruped robot, we demonstrate that our method can complete the course at half the speed of a dog. We hope that our work represents a step towards creating controllers that enable robots to reach animal-level agility.", []]
["mqe_abs", "Abstract: The advent of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has significantly advanced the field of robotics, particularly in the control and coordination of quadruped robots. However, the complexity of real-world tasks often necessitates the deployment of multi-robot systems capable of sophisticated interaction and collaboration. To address this need, we introduce the Multi-agent Quadruped Environment (MQE), a novel platform designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms in realistic and dynamic scenarios. MQE emphasizes complex interactions between robots and objects, hierarchical policy structures, and challenging evaluation scenarios that reflect real-world applications. We present a series of collaborative and competitive tasks within MQE, ranging from simple coordination to complex adversarial interactions, and benchmark state-of-the-art MARL algorithms. Our findings indicate that hierarchical reinforcement learning can simplify task learning, but also highlight the need for advanced algorithms capable of handling the intricate dynamics of multi-agent interactions. MQE serves as a stepping stone towards bridging the gap between simulation and practical deployment, offering a rich environment for future research in multi-agent systems and robot learning. For open-sourced code and more details of MQE, please refer to this https URL .", [["this https URL", "https://ziyanx02.github.io/multiagent-quadruped-environment/"], ["this https URL", "https://github.com/ziyanx02/multiagent-quadruped-environment"]]]
["rci_readme", "# Quadruped Robot Navigation in Gazebo

This repository integrates reinforcement learning (RL), navigation, and simulation to enable autonomous navigation for the Unitree Go2, Go2W and B2 quadruped robots in Gazebo.

## Overview This project follows a Sim-to-Sim approach, executing controllers trained in Isaac Lab within the Gazebo simulator. The virtual Unitree Go2, Go2W and B2 robots are equipped with a LiDAR. The mounting position of the Velodyne VLP16 LiDAR is based on the [Unitree developer documentation](https://support.unitree.com/home/en/developer/SLAM%20and%20Navigation_service).

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have the following dependencies installed:

1.  **ROS 2 Humble:** Please follow the official installation instructions.


2.  **Required ROS 2 Packages:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y \
      ros-humble-teleop-twist-keyboard \
      ros-humble-ros2-control \
      ros-humble-ros2-controllers \
      ros-humble-control-toolbox \
      ros-humble-robot-state-publisher \
      ros-humble-joint-state-publisher-gui \
      ros-humble-gazebo-ros2-control \
      ros-humble-gazebo-ros-pkgs \
      ros-humble-xacro \
      ros-humble-navigation2 \
      ros-humble-nav2-bringup \
      ros-humble-octomap-ros\
      ros-humble-octomap-rviz-plugins\
      ros-humble-velodyne-laserscan

    ```

3.  **LibTorch (C++):**
    ```bash
    # Choose a directory to store the library
    mkdir -p ~/libs && cd ~/libs
    wget https://download.pytorch.org/libtorch/cpu/libtorch-cxx11-abi-shared-with-deps-2.0.1%2Bcpu.zip
    unzip libtorch-cxx11-abi-shared-with-deps-2.0.1+cpu.zip
    rm libtorch-cxx11-abi-shared-with-deps-2.0.1+cpu.zip
    echo 'export Torch_DIR=$HOME/libs/libtorch' >> ~/.bashrc
    source ~/.bashrc
    ```

4.  **yaml-cpp and lcm:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt install -y liblcm-dev libyaml-cpp-dev
    ```

## Installation

1.  **Clone the Repository:**
    Create a ROS 2 workspace and clone this repository recursively.
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/ros2_ws/src && cd ~/ros2_ws/src
    git clone https://github.com/RCILab/RCI_quadruped_robot_navigation --recursive
    ```

2.  **Build the Workspace:**
    Install dependencies and build the packages.
    ```bash
    cd ~/ros2_ws
    colcon build --symlink-install
    ```

3.  **Source the Environment:**
    Source the workspace's setup file to make the packages available in your environment.
    ```bash
    echo "source ~/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash" >> ~/.bashrc
    source ~/.bashrc
    ```


## Usage

Follow these steps to launch the simulation and control the robot. Each command should be run in a new terminal.

1.  **Launch Gazebo & RViz2:**
    This command starts the Gazebo simulation with the robot model and launches RViz2 for visualization.
    *   Default robot is `go2`.
    *   Use the `rname` argument to switch to another robot like `go2w`.

    ```bash
    # Launch with the default Go2 robot
    ros2 launch rl_sar gazebo.launch.py

    # Launch with the Go2W robot
    ros2 launch rl_sar gazebo.launch.py rname:="go2w"

    # Launch with the Go2W robot
    ros2 launch rl_sar gazebo.launch.py rname:="b2"
    ```

2.  **Run the RL Controller:**
    This node is responsible for the robot's locomotion control.
    ```bash
    ros2 run rl_sar rl_sim
    ```

3.  **Run the Action Client:**
    This client sends high-level commands or goals to the controller.
    ```bash
    ros2 run rl_action command
    ```
    
4. Execute Navigation (Nav2)
  4.1 Convert Velodyne PointCloud2 -> LaserScan (/scan)
  ```bash
  ros2 run velodyne_laserscan velodyne_laserscan_node --ros-args \
    -r velodyne_points:=/velodyne_points \
    -r scan:=/scan
  ```
  4.2 Launch Nav2
  ```bash
  ros2 launch rl_sar nav2.launch.py
  ```
5. **Elevator Control (Optional Feature)** 
    This repository includes a Gazebo **Elevator Plugin** to simulate multi-floor vertical transport. 
    See below for detailed usage instructions.

    [elevator_operation.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f1b5e62-1e6d-4f18-85f2-8dacea8a14e9)

    #### Elevator Plugin Usage

    This plugin allows you to simulate an elevator system inside the Gazebo environment using ROS 2 topics. 
    The elevator supports floor indexing, precise height targeting, and door open/close commands.

    #### Topics

    Assuming ` / = /lift1`:

    **Commands**
    - `/lift1/cmd_floor` (`std_msgs/Int32`): floor index (0-based) from ` `
    - `/lift1/cmd_z` (`std_msgs/Float64`): absolute target height in meters
    - `/lift1/door_open` (`std_msgs/Bool`): `true` = open, `false` = close

    **Status**
    - `/lift1/cabin_z` (`std_msgs/Float64`): measured cabin Z
    - `/lift1/door_pos` (`std_msgs/Float64MultiArray`): `[right, left]` joint positions

    #### Examples Click to expand ```bash
    # Move by floor index
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/cmd_floor std_msgs/msg/Int32 "{data: 0}"
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/cmd_floor std_msgs/msg/Int32 "{data: 1}"
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/cmd_floor std_msgs/msg/Int32 "{data: 2}"

    # Move to absolute height (meters)
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/cmd_z std_msgs/msg/Float64 "{data: 3.0}"

    # Open / close doors
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/door_open std_msgs/msg/Bool "{data: true}"
    ros2 topic pub /lift1/door_open std_msgs/msg/Bool "{data: false}"

    # Monitor
    ros2 topic echo /lift1/cabin_z
    ros2 topic echo /lift1/door_pos
    ```
    
6. **Door Control (Optional Feature)**  
    This repository includes a Gazebo **Door Plugin** and a Behavior-Tree-based **Door Controller** to control doors in the simulated building via ROS 2.
    ![door_plugin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cbc78d2-b43d-4adc-a019-1a0dc1cd3005)

    The environment contains **37 doors** in total, with the following types:
    
    - Single hinged doors  
    - Single sliding doors  
    - Double hinged doors  
    - Double sliding doors  
    
    All doors share the **same topic interface**; only the **namespace** changes (e.g., `/L1_door1`, `/L1_door2`, `/L2_door5`, ...). Click to expand #### 5.1 Door Plugin Usage
    
    Each door is controlled by a dedicated namespace.  
    Below is an example for the door with namespace `/L1_door1`:
    
    #### Topics
    
    **Commands**
    - `/L1_door1/door_open` (`std_msgs/Bool`):  
      - `true`  → open the door  
      - `false` → close the door  
    
    **Status**
    - `/L1_door1/door_pos`: current door joint position(s)  
      - For double doors, this typically represents both leaves (e.g., `[right, left]`).
    
    #### Example Commands
    ```bash
    # Open / close a door (L1_door1)
    ros2 topic pub /L1_door1/door_open std_msgs/msg/Bool "{data: true}"
    ros2 topic pub /L1_door1/door_open std_msgs/msg/Bool "{data: false}"
    
    # Monitor door joint position(s)
    ros2 topic echo /L1_door1/door_pos
    ```
    To control **any other door**, simply replace L1_door1 with the corresponding door namespace
    (e.g., `/L1_door2`, `/L1_door_stairs1`, `/L1_door_toilet`, `/L2_door3`, etc.).

For the first time, we systematically evaluate several ego-centric VLN methods in physical robotic settings across different technical pipelines, including classification models for single-step discrete action prediction, a diffusion model for dense waypoint prediction, and a train-free, map-based large language model (LLM) integrated with path planning. ["navila_abs", "Abstract: This paper proposes to solve the problem of Vision-and-Language Navigation with legged robots, which not only provides a flexible way for humans to command but also allows the robot to navigate through more challenging and cluttered scenes. However, it is non-trivial to translate human language instructions all the way to low-level leg joint actions. We propose NaVILA, a 2-level framework that unifies a Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) with locomotion skills. Instead of directly predicting low-level actions from VLA, NaVILA first generates mid-level actions with spatial information in the form of language, (e.g., \"moving forward 75cm\"), which serves as an input for a visual locomotion RL policy for execution. NaVILA substantially improves previous approaches on existing benchmarks. The same advantages are demonstrated in our newly developed benchmarks with IsaacLab, featuring more realistic scenes, low-level controls, and real-world robot experiments. We show more results at this https URL", [["this https URL", "https://navila-bot.github.io/"], ["this https URL", "https://navila-bot.github.io/"]]]
["barkour_abs", "Abstract: Animals have evolved various agile locomotion strategies, such as sprinting, leaping, and jumping. There is a growing interest in developing legged robots that move like their biological counterparts and show various agile skills to navigate complex environments quickly. Despite the interest, the field lacks systematic benchmarks to measure the performance of control policies and hardware in agility. We introduce the Barkour benchmark, an obstacle course to quantify agility for legged robots. Inspired by dog agility competitions, it consists of diverse obstacles and a time based scoring mechanism. This encourages researchers to develop controllers that not only move fast, but do so in a controllable and versatile way. To set strong baselines, we present two methods for tackling the benchmark. In the first approach, we train specialist locomotion skills using on-policy reinforcement learning methods and combine them with a high-level navigation controller. In the second approach, we distill the specialist skills into a Transformer-based generalist locomotion policy, named Locomotion-Transformer, that can handle various terrains and adjust the robot's gait based on the perceived environment and robot states. Using a custom-built quadruped robot, we demonstrate that our method can complete the course at half the speed of a dog. We hope that our work represents a step towards creating controllers that enable robots to reach animal-level agility.", []]
["mqe_abs", "Abstract: The advent of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has significantly advanced the field of robotics, particularly in the control and coordination of quadruped robots. However, the complexity of real-world tasks often necessitates the deployment of multi-robot systems capable of sophisticated interaction and collaboration. To address this need, we introduce the Multi-agent Quadruped Environment (MQE), a novel platform designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms in realistic and dynamic scenarios. MQE emphasizes complex interactions between robots and objects, hierarchical policy structures, and challenging evaluation scenarios that reflect real-world applications. We present a series of collaborative and competitive tasks within MQE, ranging from simple coordination to complex adversarial interactions, and benchmark state-of-the-art MARL algorithms. Our findings indicate that hierarchical reinforcement learning can simplify task learning, but also highlight the need for advanced algorithms capable of handling the intricate dynamics of multi-agent interactions. MQE serves as a stepping stone towards bridging the gap between simulation and practical deployment, offering a rich environment for future research in multi-agent systems and robot learning. ["vlnpe_page", "Rethinking the Embodied Gap in Vision-and-Language Navigation: A Holistic Study of Physical and Visual Disparities Rethinking the Embodied Gap in Vision-and-Language Navigation: A Holistic Study of Physical and Visual Disparities Liuyi Wang 1,2* , Xinyuan Xia 2,3* , Hui Zhao 2 , Hanqing Wang 2+ , Tai Wang 2 , Yilun Chen 2 , Chengju Liu 1,4 , Qijun Chen 1,4+ , Jiangmiao Pang 2 1 Tongji University, 2 Shanghai AI Laboratory, 3 Shanghai Jiao Tong University 4 State Key Laboratory of Autonomous Intelligent Unmanned Systems * Equal Contribution + Corresponding Author Paper Code arXiv 🤖 Different viewpoints of the robots walking in VLN-PE. 🗺️ Trajectories and instructions from the GRU-VLN10 dataset. 🏢 Trajectories and instructions from the 3DGS-Lab-VLN dataset. 💡 Comparisons of different lighting conditions. We introduce VLN-PE, a realistic VLN platform and benchmark designed to enhance physical deployment across diverse robot embodiments. It enables cross-embodiment data collection, evaluation, and optimization under realistic locomotion and environmental conditions. Through systematic experiments on ego-centric VLN methods, we expose critical physical and visual disparities that challenge existing approaches and benchmarks. VLN-PE offers a grounded framework to foster more generalizable VLN models for future physical embodied AI development. Abstract Recent Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) advancements are promising, but their idealized assumptions about robot movement and control fail to reflect physically embodied deployment challenges. To bridge this gap, we introduce VLN-PE, a physically realistic VLN platform supporting humanoid, quadruped, and wheeled robots. For the first time, we systematically evaluate several ego-centric VLN methods in physical robotic settings across different technical pipelines, including classification models for single-step discrete action prediction, a diffusion model for dense waypoint prediction, and a train-free, map-based large language model (LLM) integrated with path planning. Our results reveal significant performance degradation due to limited robot observation space, environmental lighting variations, and physical challenges like collisions and falls. This also exposes locomotion constraints for legged robots in complex environments. VLN-PE is highly extensible, allowing seamless integration of new scenes beyond MP3D, thereby enabling more comprehensive VLN evaluation. Despite the weak generalization of current models in physical deployment, VLN-PE provides a new pathway for improving cross-embodiment's overall adaptability. We hope our findings and tools inspire the community to rethink VLN limitations and advance robust, practical VLN models. ["mqe_page", "MQE: Unleashing the Power of Interaction with Multi-agent Quadruped Environment MQE: Unleashing the Power of Interaction with M ulti-agent Q uadruped E nvironment Ziyan Xiong 1 , Bo Chen 2 , Shiyu Huang 3 , Wei-Wei Tu 4 , Zhaofeng He 2 , Yang Gao 156 1 Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences, Tsinghua University 2 AI Institute, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunication 3 Zhipu AI, 4 4Paradigm Inc., 5 Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute 6 Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Paper Code Agents try to herd sheep in parallel simulation created by MQE Abstract The advent of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has significantly advanced the field of robotics, 
            particularly in the control and coordination of quadruped robots. However, the complexity of real-world 
            tasks often necessitates the deployment of multi-robot systems capable of sophisticated interaction 
            and collaboration. To address this need, we introduce the Multi-agent Quadruped Environment (MQE), 
            a novel platform designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) 
            algorithms in realistic and dynamic scenarios. MQE emphasizes complex interactions between robots and objects, hierarchical 
            policy structures, and challenging evaluation scenarios that reflect real-world applications. 
            We present a series of collaborative and competitive tasks within MQE, ranging from simple 
            coordination to complex adversarial interactions, and benchmark state-of-the-art MARL algorithms. Our findings indicate 
            that hierarchical reinforcement learning can simplify task learning, but also highlight the need for advanced algorithms 
            capable of handling the intricate dynamics of multi-agent interactions. MQE serves as a stepping stone towards bridging the 
            gap between simulation and practical deployment, offering a rich environment for future research in multi-agent systems and robot learning. Chase Kew * , Tingnan Zhang * , Daniel Freeman¹, Kuang-Huei Lee ¹ , Lisa Lee¹, Stefano Saliceti¹, Vincent Zhuang¹, Nathan Batchelor, Steven Bohez, Federico Casarini, Jose Enrique Chen, Omar Cortes, Erwin Coumans^, Adil Dostmohamed, Gabriel Dulac-Arnold, Alejandro Escontrela^, Erik Frey, Roland Hafner, Deepali Jain, Bauyrjan Jyenis, Yuheng Kuang, Edward Lee, Linda Luu, Ofir Nachum, Ken Oslund, Jason Powell, Diego Reyes, Francesco Romano, Fereshteh Sadeghi, Ron Sloat, Baruch Tabanpour, Daniel Zheng, Michael Neunert, Raia Hadsell, Nicolas Heess, Francesco Nori, Jeff Seto, Carolina Parada, Vikas Sindhwani, Vincent Vanhoucke, and Jie Tan (*equal contribution ¹core contributor    ^work done while at Google) Google DeepMind Paper Google AI Blog Open- S ourced Assets Animals have evolved various agile locomotion strategies, such as sprinting, leaping, and jumping. There is a growing interest in developing legged robots that move like their biological counterparts and show various agile skills to navigate complex environments quickly. Despite the interest, the field lacks systematic benchmarks to measure the performance of control policies and hardware in agility. We introduce the Barkour benchmark, an obstacle course to quantify agility for legged robots.  Inspired by dog agility competitions, it consists of diverse obstacles and a time based scoring mechanism. This encourages researchers to develop controllers that not only move fast, but do so in a controllable and versatile way. To set strong baselines, we present two methods for tackling the benchmark. In the first approach, we train specialist locomotion skills using on-policy reinforcement learning methods and combine them with a high-level navigation controller. In the second approach, we distill the specialist skills into a Transformer-based generalist locomotion policy, named Locomotion-Transformer, that can handle various terrains and adjust the robot's gait based on the perceived environment and robot states. ["robotworld_hf", "Paper page - RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments Papers arxiv:2610.10409 Copy markdown RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments Published on Oct 7 · Submitted by zhiqin yang on Oct 8 Upvote 40 +32 Authors: Zhiqin Yang , Chenxin Li , Xiaomeng Hu , Yibin Liu , Weidong Huang , Jiankai Sun , Haitao Li , Zijian Wu , Yuzhi Huang , Fanding Huang , Hanwen Sun , Jiashun Liu , Jingqi Tong , Mingxin Huang , Shaoli Hu , Shijue Huang , Tianyi Bai , Xinyuan Wang , Yunlong Lin , Zhengyang Tang , Zhexin Zhang , Zhuo Chen + 11 authors Abstract RobotWorld evaluates general-purpose agents on physical robot tasks, revealing transferable perception and control skills but persistent gaps in reliable execution and task completion. Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small General-purpose agents increasingly write code, use tools, and complete complex digital tasks, raising the question of how far these capabilities carry into the physical world. To investigate this, we introduce RobotWorld , a challenging simulation testbed for robot use : turning instructions and observations into physical task execution through robot interfaces. Its 84 tasks span manipulation , mobile manipulation , locomotion , driving , and aerial control , with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. By analysing task outcomes alongside execution traces, we identify both the capabilities that transfer and the gaps that prevent reliable completion. Furthermore, we find that current agents can construct sophisticated perception and control workflows, including image segmentation , camera calibration , spatial estimation , and dynamics-based computation . These capabilities, however, do not consistently compose into successful behaviour: agents lose task-relevant object states despite reaching commanded poses, fail to correct ineffective actions, recover too late, or mistake unfinished tasks for completion. This uneven transfer also differs across models: Astra succeeds more often on spatial and constrained-contact goals , whereas Opus 5.5 succeeds more often on continuous-balance and timed-interaction goals. By linking these outcomes to execution behaviour, RobotWorld provides both a rigorous proving ground and an empirical account of the remaining capability gaps, thereby establishing concrete targets for training and designing more reliable physical-world agents. Abstract Recent Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) advancements are promising, but their idealized assumptions about robot movement and control fail to reflect physically embodied deployment challenges. Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small General-purpose agents increasingly write code, use tools, and complete complex digital tasks, raising the question of how far these capabilities carry into the physical world. To investigate this, we introduce RobotWorld , a challenging simulation testbed for robot use : turning instructions and observations into physical task execution through robot interfaces. Its 84 tasks span manipulation , mobile manipulation , locomotion , driving , and aerial control , with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. By analysing task outcomes alongside execution traces, we identify both the capabilities that transfer and the gaps that prevent reliable completion. Furthermore, we find that current agents can construct sophisticated perception and control workflows, including image segmentation , camera calibration , spatial estimation , and dynamics-based computation . These capabilities, however, do not consistently compose into successful behaviour: agents lose task-relevant object states despite reaching commanded poses, fail to correct ineffective actions, recover too late, or mistake unfinished tasks for completion. This uneven transfer also differs across models: Astra succeeds more often on spatial and constrained-contact goals , whereas Opus 5.5 succeeds more often on continuous-balance and timed-interaction goals. By linking these outcomes to execution behaviour, RobotWorld provides both a rigorous proving ground and an empirical account of the remaining capability gaps, thereby establishing concrete targets for training and designing more reliable physical-world agents. --- ## ✨ What Is RobotWorld? RobotWorld connects a source-built multimodal agent runtime to robot simulators through explicit observation and action interfaces. Agents can analyse observations, issue bounded robot commands, and use execution feedback to revise their actions. Task evaluators assess the resulting trajectories independently of the agent's completion claims. This source snapshot registers **84 tasks across 20 benchmark integrations**. Registration does not imply that every task has a verified successful physical trajectory. The default batch protocol runs three rollouts per task with environment-side code control disabled. Simulation pauses during agent reasoning and workspace analysis. ## Quick Start Start with one RoboCasa task before provisioning the full suite. You need a Linux/NVIDIA host, Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Python 3.11+, and the pinned build dependencies. **L40S 48GB is the current host reference, not an all-task compatibility guarantee.** See the [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) for prerequisites and troubleshooting.
GPU compatibility and host dependencies ### Hardware and dependencies - **Current host reference:** NVIDIA L40S 48GB (driver `580.105.08`); this describes the deployment host, not certification of all 84 tasks. - **Other GPUs:** RTX 5090 has historical partial-task validation with experimental Isaac Sim 6.0.1 profiles; older Isaac/CUDA stacks can be incompatible. RTX 4090, RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada and L40 are RT-capable candidates, not a verified support list. - **Isaac rendering:** use a GPU with RT Cores. A100/H100 are [not supported by Isaac Sim](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/requirements.html), although they can host a separate model inference service. With a remote model API, local GPUs primarily run simulation and rendering. - **Compatibility:** match the task's pinned image, driver and CUDA/Isaac versions, then run a smoke episode before scaling. No suite-wide minimum VRAM, RAM or disk requirement has been established. Host dependencies: Linux, a compatible NVIDIA driver, Docker with Compose/Buildx and NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Git/Git LFS, Python 3.11+, the pinned Rust toolchain, C/C++ build tools (CMake, Clang and OpenSSL headers), bubblewrap with user namespaces, FFmpeg/ffprobe and zstd. Provision the pinned simulator images and assets, including any required access or licences; see the [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).
### 1. Prepare one environment Run these commands from the repository root after cloning. Restore pinned sources **before** assets. ```bash git clone https://github.com/robotworldai/robotworld.git cd robotworld python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e '.[test]' huggingface_hub export WORLD_PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh sources # Authenticate with your own account if asset access requires it. hf auth login bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh assets --bench robocasa bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh docker --bench robocasa --dry-run bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh docker --bench robocasa bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh codex ``` You can [import prebuilt images](docs/PREBUILT_IMAGES.md) instead of building them; access currently requires authorisation, and some legacy profiles need additional images. For runtime helper build failures, see the [direct-tool option](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#direct-tool-runtime-option). Other environments may require additional assets, base images and licences. ### 2. Connect a model and run one task Use a reachable streaming **Responses API** endpoint with image and function-call support. A Chat Completions-only endpoint is not sufficient. ```bash python scripts/configure_api.py \ --base-url https://YOUR_API_HOST/v1 \ --model YOUR_MULTIMODAL_MODEL_ID export CODEX_AUTH_HOME="$PWD/var/auth/api" # Read the key without echoing it or saving it in shell history. read -rsp "Model API key: " WORLD_MODEL_API_KEY; printf '\n' export WORLD_MODEL_API_KEY python scripts/check_api.py bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh list bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --tasks CloseDrawer --rollouts 1 --dry-run bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --tasks CloseDrawer --rollouts 1 --batch drawer-smoke ``` Replace the endpoint and model placeholders with your provider's values. The API check makes two small paid model requests, but does not start a simulator. Configuration stores the credential variable's name, not its value. In a new shell, reactivate the virtual environment and restore the environment variables. ### 3. Inspect results, then scale up Inspect `run.json`, videos and events under `outputs/robocasa/CloseDrawer/`. A valid task failure is `false`; infrastructure or indeterminate outcomes are unscored (`null`). Preserve the whole run directory, including `artifacts/`, when archiving. ```bash # Run all RoboCasa tasks, three trials per task. ROLLOUTS=3 bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --batch model-a-01 # Retry unfinished slots with the same settings. ROLLOUTS=3 bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --batch model-a-01 --resume ``` **Current defaults:** 3 rollouts per task, environment-side `code_control=off`, per-task control-step budgets, and `--timeout=43200` (12 hours). Simulation pauses during reasoning; offline analysis is still allowed. Native termination conditions remain active. `--resume` starts unfinished rollouts from the initial state, not a saved physics state. Use a new batch ID when changing evaluation conditions. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | | --- | --- | | [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) | Host setup, sources, runtime builds and troubleshooting | | [Assets](docs/ASSETS.md) / [Prebuilt images](docs/PREBUILT_IMAGES.md) | Pinned downloads, access and licences | | [Model API](docs/MODELS.md) | Providers, credentials and model configuration | | [Evaluation](scripts/ROLLOUTS.md) | Task budgets, control modes, full-suite runs, resume and metrics | | [Repository layout](DIRECTORY_GUIDE.md) | Source and output directory map | | [Release boundaries](docs/HANDOFF.md) / [Checks](docs/RELEASE_REVIEW.md) | Reproducibility limits and recorded validation | ## Release Status The release documentation records outstanding full-suite test failures and pending API-backed simulator validation. Historical trajectories are not a fresh validation of this source release; validate your chosen environment before scaling. Third-party code and assets retain their own licences. BEHAVIOR assets and decryption keys are not redistributed. **A top-level licence for RobotWorld-owned code has not yet been selected.**

--- ## ✨ What Is RobotWorld? RobotWorld connects a source-built multimodal agent runtime to robot simulators through explicit observation and action interfaces. Agents can analyse observations, issue bounded robot commands, and use execution feedback to revise their actions. Task evaluators assess the resulting trajectories independently of the agent's completion claims. This source snapshot registers **84 tasks across 20 benchmark integrations**. Registration does not imply that every task has a verified successful physical trajectory. The default batch protocol runs three rollouts per task with environment-side code control disabled. Simulation pauses during agent reasoning and workspace analysis. ## Quick Start Start with one RoboCasa task before provisioning the full suite. You need a Linux/NVIDIA host, Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Python 3.11+, and the pinned build dependencies. **L40S 48GB is the current host reference, not an all-task compatibility guarantee.** See the [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) for prerequisites and troubleshooting.
GPU compatibility and host dependencies ### Hardware and dependencies - **Current host reference:** NVIDIA L40S 48GB (driver `580.105.08`); this describes the deployment host, not certification of all 84 tasks. - **Other GPUs:** RTX 5090 has historical partial-task validation with experimental Isaac Sim 6.0.1 profiles; older Isaac/CUDA stacks can be incompatible. RTX 4090, RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada and L40 are RT-capable candidates, not a verified support list. - **Isaac rendering:** use a GPU with RT Cores. A100/H100 are [not supported by Isaac Sim](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/requirements.html), although they can host a separate model inference service. With a remote model API, local GPUs primarily run simulation and rendering. - **Compatibility:** match the task's pinned image, driver and CUDA/Isaac versions, then run a smoke episode before scaling. No suite-wide minimum VRAM, RAM or disk requirement has been established. Host dependencies: Linux, a compatible NVIDIA driver, Docker with Compose/Buildx and NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Git/Git LFS, Python 3.11+, the pinned Rust toolchain, C/C++ build tools (CMake, Clang and OpenSSL headers), bubblewrap with user namespaces, FFmpeg/ffprobe and zstd. Provision the pinned simulator images and assets, including any required access or licences; see the [deployment guide](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).
### 1. Prepare one environment Run these commands from the repository root after cloning. Restore pinned sources **before** assets. ```bash git clone https://github.com/robotworldai/robotworld.git cd robotworld python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e '.[test]' huggingface_hub export WORLD_PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh sources # Authenticate with your own account if asset access requires it. hf auth login bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh assets --bench robocasa bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh docker --bench robocasa --dry-run bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh docker --bench robocasa bash scripts/setup_handoff.sh codex ``` You can [import prebuilt images](docs/PREBUILT_IMAGES.md) instead of building them; access currently requires authorisation, and some legacy profiles need additional images. For runtime helper build failures, see the [direct-tool option](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#direct-tool-runtime-option). Other environments may require additional assets, base images and licences. ### 2. Connect a model and run one task Use a reachable streaming **Responses API** endpoint with image and function-call support. A Chat Completions-only endpoint is not sufficient. ```bash python scripts/configure_api.py \ --base-url https://YOUR_API_HOST/v1 \ --model YOUR_MULTIMODAL_MODEL_ID export CODEX_AUTH_HOME="$PWD/var/auth/api" # Read the key without echoing it or saving it in shell history. read -rsp "Model API key: " WORLD_MODEL_API_KEY; printf '\n' export WORLD_MODEL_API_KEY python scripts/check_api.py bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh list bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --tasks CloseDrawer --rollouts 1 --dry-run bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --tasks CloseDrawer --rollouts 1 --batch drawer-smoke ``` Replace the endpoint and model placeholders with your provider's values. The API check makes two small paid model requests, but does not start a simulator. Configuration stores the credential variable's name, not its value. In a new shell, reactivate the virtual environment and restore the environment variables. ### 3. Inspect results, then scale up Inspect `run.json`, videos and events under `outputs/robocasa/CloseDrawer/`. A valid task failure is `false`; infrastructure or indeterminate outcomes are unscored (`null`). Preserve the whole run directory, including `artifacts/`, when archiving. ```bash # Run all RoboCasa tasks, three trials per task. ROLLOUTS=3 bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --batch model-a-01 # Retry unfinished slots with the same settings. ROLLOUTS=3 bash scripts/run_robocasa.sh run --batch model-a-01 --resume ``` **Current defaults:** 3 rollouts per task, environment-side `code_control=off`, per-task control-step budgets, and `--timeout=43200` (12 hours). Simulation pauses during reasoning; offline analysis is still allowed. Native termination conditions remain active. `--resume` starts unfinished rollouts from the initial state, not a saved physics state. Use a new batch ID when changing evaluation conditions. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | | --- | --- | | [Deployment](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) | Host setup, sources, runtime builds and troubleshooting | | [Assets](docs/ASSETS.md) / [Prebuilt images](docs/PREBUILT_IMAGES.md) | Pinned downloads, access and licences | | [Model API](docs/MODELS.md) | Providers, credentials and model configuration | | [Evaluation](scripts/ROLLOUTS.md) | Task budgets, control modes, full-suite runs, resume and metrics | | [Repository layout](DIRECTORY_GUIDE.md) | Source and output directory map | | [Release boundaries](docs/HANDOFF.md) / [Checks](docs/RELEASE_REVIEW.md) | Reproducibility limits and recorded validation | ## Release Status The release documentation records outstanding full-suite test failures and pending API-backed simulator validation. Historical trajectories are not a fresh validation of this source release; validate your chosen environment before scaling. Third-party code and assets retain their own licences. BEHAVIOR assets and decryption keys are not redistributed. **A top-level licence for RobotWorld-owned code has not yet been selected.**
Source provenance and validation scope The source for this release is `visitworld123/RoboWorld_Scaffold`, branch `main`, commit `132972eec7ea4e9a5b59f8be7398f19d7681fc52`. Run CPU tests with `python -m pytest`. Task lists, dry runs and API checks do not replace GPU rollout validation. Experimental Isaac compatibility layers are recorded in run metadata and do not establish equivalence to the original simulator.

["dped_repo", "# DPedVLN

Official code for "DPed-VLN: A Benchmark for Socially Compliant Vision-and-Language Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments".

## News

- 2026-09: The DPed-VLN dataset is released on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22816620
- Code release: we are cleaning up the internal repository and will push it here shortly.

## Overview

DPed-VLN is a Habitat 3.0 benchmark for vision-and-language navigation with dynamic pedestrians. It contains 33,093 navigation episodes (32,172 train / 921 val-unseen), each paired with a level-1 global instruction and a level-2 prior-augmented instruction, giving 66,186 instruction-trajectory pairs in total. Pedestrians are ORCA-controlled humanoids, and expert trajectories are generated by a hybrid planner that combines global shortest-path intent with local pedestrian avoidance. Evaluation covers both navigation efficiency (SR, SPL, STL) and social safety (HCR, PSC).

This repository will include:

1. DPet baseline, with RL and IL training configs
2. Evaluation code for all reported metrics

## Dataset

The dataset is hosted on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22816620

*** Add File: D:/Project/AgenticCyberDog/docs/benchmark-survey-2026-10-21.md
+# 适合 Agent4CyberDog 的 Benchmark 调研
+
+检索日期：2026-10-21（Asia/Shanghai）。检索入口包括 papers.cool、arXiv 和用户提供的 Awesome-Astra-Embodied-AI，结论主要依据论文原文、官方项目页与官方代码。此次做了资料和源码检查，没有安装仿真器、运行基线或操作真机。本文独立于原有 Survey 模板，包含针对当前问题的选型建议。
+
+**结论：有合适的 benchmark，但没有在本轮核实到能直接对 CyberDog 一键完整评测的标准套件。** 优先考虑 VLN-CE-Isaac / NaVILA 和 VLN-PE；RobotWorld 最贴近通用 agent 控制机器人的研究问题；Barkour 用来评价底层运动能力。选型建议是研究判断，不代表已在你们的设备上复现。
+
+**1. 先明确“控制水平”指什么**
+
+| 层次 | 典型任务 | 适合的评测 | 分数主要反映什么 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 底层运动 | 速度跟踪、抗扰恢复、越障 | Barkour；RobotWorld 的部分关节控制任务 | 控制策略与机器人本体共同决定的运动能力 |
+| 导航与身体约束 | 按语言走路线、穿门、避障、寻找物体 | VLN-PE、VLN-CE-Isaac、ObjectNav | 感知、导航决策与运动执行的组合能力 |
+| Agent 任务执行 | 理解任务、使用接口、记住状态、发现失败并恢复 | RobotWorld 的协议；在导航任务上增加独立评测器 | 模型与工具接口、上下文、底层控制器共同构成的系统能力 |
+
+如果项目主要让 Astra/Codex 调用已有运动接口，建议首先固定底层控制器，比较不同 agent 的导航和任务执行。若同时更换 agent、定位系统、运动策略和传感器，成绩变化很难归因。四足专用运动评测虽然有较早的论文，仍然值得保留；新 agent 可以在旧而明确的协议上被评测。
+
+**2. 值得优先研究的六组候选**
+

+**先做两个仿真层次，再做一套少量可重复的真机任务。**

+1. **比较高层 agent：** 采用固定版本 ObjectNav / R2R / RxR episodes，给模型相同图像、工具、记忆和调用预算。固定导航动作执行层，报告 SR、SPL、STOP 误判和成本。这能先看清语言理解、搜索和规划差异。

+| 绕障到达目标；原路线受阻后重规划 | 身体尺寸意识、反馈与恢复 | 到达情况、碰撞/卡住、绕行距离、恢复次数、人工接管 |

+第一版可以采用 **5 类任务 × 4 个固定初始布置 × 3 次重复 = 每模型 60 次尝试**，这是便于组织的试验提案，不是统计功效保证；正式比较应根据方差增加种子/重复并报告置信区间。固定起点、场景、成功阈值、动作边界、底层控制器、模型版本及预算，保存失败和超时。
+
+建议设置固定规则/状态机或经典规划基线，以及使用同一工具与运动层的模型基线。脚本基线拿到额外地图或真值时，应明确其额外信息，不与 RGB-only agent 混报。

+若要测接口自学，可沿用此前讨论的 **D0 / D1 / D2** 区分：不给具体接口提示、给接口说明、给最小示例。它是独立实验变量，不应与“是否有动作技能/记忆/反馈”混成同一个条件。本轮只引用该历史设计思路，未重新检查机器人当前接口或旧实验完成情况。

# 适合 Agent4CyberDog 的 Benchmark 调研

检索日期：2026-10-21（Asia/Shanghai）。检索入口包括 papers.cool、arXiv 和用户提供的 Awesome-Astra-Embodied-AI，结论主要依据论文原文、官方项目页与官方代码。此次做了资料和源码检查，没有安装仿真器、运行基线或操作真机。本文独立于原有 Survey 模板，包含针对当前问题的选型建议。

**结论：有合适的 benchmark，但没有在本轮核实到能直接对 CyberDog 一键完整评测的标准套件。** 优先考虑 VLN-CE-Isaac / NaVILA 和 VLN-PE；RobotWorld 最贴近通用 agent 控制机器人的研究问题；Barkour 用来评价底层运动能力。选型建议是研究判断，不代表已在你们的设备上复现。

**1. 先明确“控制水平”指什么**

| 层次 | 典型任务 | 适合的评测 | 分数主要反映什么 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 底层运动 | 速度跟踪、抗扰恢复、越障 | Barkour；RobotWorld 的部分关节控制任务 | 控制策略与机器人本体共同决定的运动能力 |
| 导航与身体约束 | 按语言走路线、穿门、避障、寻找物体 | VLN-PE、VLN-CE-Isaac、ObjectNav | 感知、导航决策与运动执行的组合能力 |
| Agent 任务执行 | 理解任务、使用接口、记住状态、发现失败并恢复 | RobotWorld 的协议；在导航任务上增加独立评测器 | 模型与工具接口、上下文、底层控制器共同构成的系统能力 |

如果项目主要让 Astra/Codex 调用已有运动接口，建议首先固定底层控制器，比较不同 agent 的导航和任务执行。若同时更换 agent、定位系统、运动策略和传感器，成绩变化很难归因。四足专用运动评测虽然有较早的论文，仍然值得保留；新 agent 可以在旧而明确的协议上被评测。

**3. 复现成本中最容易忽略的几点**

- **VLN-CE-Isaac：** README 固定 Isaac Sim 4.1.0、修改版 Isaac Lab 1.1.0、Python 3.10，并明确提示新版兼容性未知。文档要求 NaVILA VLA 评测使用至少 24 GB 显存，也支持把 VLM 服务放到另一台机器。这个显存要求针对其模型评测配置，不代表所有外部 API agent 都必须本地加载 NaVILA。
- **VLN-PE / InternNav：** 当前 InternNav 已扩展成较大的导航工具箱。复现原论文应锁定对应配置、版本和数据，不能把当前仓库里另一个模型/榜单的数字当成 VLN-PE 原论文结果。主平台利用 Isaac Sim / GRUtopia 的物理与渲染能力。
- **RobotWorld：** 当前 README 说明仍有完整套件测试失败和 API 驱动仿真验证待完成；顶层自有代码许可证尚未选定，部分预构建镜像需要授权。L40S 48 GB 是参考主机，不是全套任务的已验证最低要求。它非常相关，但不宜描述成“一键成熟复现”。
- **MQE：** 依赖较早的 Isaac Gym/PyTorch 栈；官方推荐 Python 3.8。任务本身适合借鉴，环境维护工作不能忽略。
- **Habitat / VLN-CE：** 原 VLN-CE 仓库依赖旧版本 Habitat；场景、任务数据和代码各自有获取与使用条件。采用更新封装时需记录版本和动作语义。

**4. 能用来讨论的公开结果：不是统一 SOTA 排名**

以下全部是作者报告，本次没有独立复现；所读材料也没有为这些具体数字建立第三方复现证据。不同表中的场景、传感器、动作接口、成功阈值、模型训练数据和预算不一致，不应横向排名。

| 来源与协议 | 作者报告结果 | 可支持的判断与限制 |

| NaVILA，§III-D / Table VI 的 Go2 真机设置；25 条指令，每条重复 3 次，涵盖 workspace/home/outdoor | 正文总结总体 SR **88%**，复杂指令 SR **75%** | 证明分层语言导航已在四足真机上有重复试验；这是作者自建任务集，不能直接与 R2R/RxR 或 CyberDog 成功率比较 |

[NaVILA 全文](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.04453v2) · [VLN-PE 全文](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.13019v2) · [Astra 报告全文](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.38537v1) · [RobotWorld 全文](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.10409v1)

**Astra 导航结果的协议尤其需要保留。** 上述报告使用单张前向 512×384 RGB 图像，不提供 GPS、指南针、深度、目标坐标等；动作适配为 0.25 m 前进和 30° 转向，预算 500 个 primitive。VLN 成功要求 STOP 距目标 3 m 内；ObjectNav 使用距离标注目标视点集合严格小于 1 m，并不要求最终图像可见物体；HM3D 依照该阈值重新评分。其 Table 8 还调整了基线的视角与动作适配，不能把 92% / 82% 当作官方全测试集榜单纪录。

**暂停仿真不等于实时控制。** Astra 报告中一个 30 秒运动运行用了 250 次模型调用，平均每次 39.86 秒，推理时物理暂停；RobotWorld 也暂停物理等待 agent。真实机器人评测应另报墙钟时间、动作完成等待、观察新鲜度、碰撞/接管，并区分停止观察式任务与连续动态控制。

**5. 三个补充方向，以及群里提到的仓库**

| 条目 | 本轮判断 |
|---|---|
| **DPed-VLN**，Haojie Dai 等，2026-09，[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21504) / [仓库](https://github.com/tju-dhj/DPedVLN) | 很适合后续研究人群中的语言导航。Habitat 3.0，33,093 episodes，含导航效率和社会安全指标。**当前 README 明确写着代码仍在整理、将随后发布**；数据已有发布入口。因此列为关注项，不列为立即完整复现首选。不是四足动力学 benchmark |
| **MimicAgent**，2026-09，[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24145) | Prompt → 参考轨迹 → 模仿式 RL → 四足技能，适合研究 agent 帮助产生新技能。摘要的 **87%** 指 prompt 生成语义对齐参考轨迹的比例，不是 87% 真机任务成功率。它是技能生成方法及实验，不是现成 CyberDog 在线控制排行榜 |
| **RoboDawn**，2026-09，[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22966) | 观察、动作、执行反馈接口的设计参考；本轮未核验到现成四足适配器。不要仅因能接入机器人控制就把它写成 CyberDog 专用 benchmark |
| **RCI_quadruped_robot_navigation**，[仓库](https://github.com/RCILab/RCI_quadruped_robot_navigation) | README 的核心是 Go2/Go2W/B2、Gazebo、ROS 2 Humble、RL 运动控制与 Nav2，还含门/电梯插件。本轮查看的 README 未给出完整固定任务列表、统一评分协议和基线成绩表。它可作为搭建环境的基础；要形成 benchmark 还需补 episodes、终止条件、指标和基线。插件开门也不能当成机器狗物理开门能力 |

**6. 给科协的具体推进建议**

**先做两个仿真层次，再做一套少量可重复的真机任务。**

1. **比较高层 agent：** 采用固定版本 ObjectNav / R2R / RxR episodes，给模型相同图像、工具、记忆和调用预算。固定导航动作执行层，报告 SR、SPL、STOP 误判和成本。这能先看清语言理解、搜索和规划差异。
2. **加入四足身体：** 在 VLN-CE-Isaac 或 VLN-PE 上采用现成四足和同一低层策略，比较 agent。记录跌倒、卡住、路径执行误差。先复现所选仓库的一条基线，再接入新模型；这一顺序避免把环境故障当作 agent 失败。
3. **迁移到 CyberDog：** 保留其已有运动控制能力，在真实相机、定位和执行接口上重新标定。以下任务与指标属于我们的提案，不是原论文已有标准。

| 提议的真机任务 | 测什么 | 建议的独立判定 |
|---|---|---|
| 定距移动、定角转向、回到起点 | 是否理解动作效果与坐标 | 外部标记/相机测量的位置和朝向误差；控制命令返回成功不能替代位姿证据 |
| 按语言依次经过若干地标 | 指令理解、顺序执行、路径规划 | 检查点顺序、最终误差、任务成功率、路径效率 |
| 找到指定物体并停在指定区域 | 主动搜索、识别和停止 | 外部位置与目标身份检查；分别记录找到、接近、停对位置，避免只凭自报成功 |
| 绕障到达目标；原路线受阻后重规划 | 身体尺寸意识、反馈与恢复 | 到达情况、碰撞/卡住、绕行距离、恢复次数、人工接管 |
| 推球到目标区域 | 接触理解、动作效果预测与闭环修正 | 球位移、最终区域误差、有效接触、越界；使用外部视频/标记判定 |

第一版可以采用 **5 类任务 × 4 个固定初始布置 × 3 次重复 = 每模型 60 次尝试**，这是便于组织的试验提案，不是统计功效保证；正式比较应根据方差增加种子/重复并报告置信区间。固定起点、场景、成功阈值、动作边界、底层控制器、模型版本及预算，保存失败和超时。

建议设置固定规则/状态机或经典规划基线，以及使用同一工具与运动层的模型基线。脚本基线拿到额外地图或真值时，应明确其额外信息，不与 RGB-only agent 混报。

若要测接口自学，可沿用此前讨论的 **D0 / D1 / D2** 区分：不给具体接口提示、给接口说明、给最小示例。它是独立实验变量，不应与“是否有动作技能/记忆/反馈”混成同一个条件。本轮只引用该历史设计思路，未重新检查机器人当前接口或旧实验完成情况。

**7. 可直接转发到群里的摘要**

> 找到了几组和狗平台相关的 benchmark。优先看 NaVILA 的 VLN-CE-Isaac（有 Go2、数据、低层策略和评测脚本）及 VLN-PE（将语言导航放到真实物理身体里，统计跌倒、卡住等），它们比单纯 Gazebo 导航环境更接近完整评测。RobotWorld 是 2026 年很贴近 agent 控制机器人的跨本体评测，包含 Go2 抗推、ANYmal 地形等任务，但当前公开版本还有复现验证缺口。若评价底层运动能力可参考 Barkour；推球、推箱和多狗交互可参考 MQE。建议固定底层控制器，把“听懂并完成任务”和“机器狗本身会不会走”分层测，再做一套有外部成功判定的小规模 CyberDog 真机任务。

+# Agent4CyberDog Benchmark 清单
+
+整理日期：2026-10-21。
+
+本清单按 Agent4CyberDog 的适用程度整理。“对应部分”指值得复用的具体任务或评测模块。以下属于资料与代码核查结论，尚未在 CyberDog 上实测。
+
+| Benchmark | 适合机器狗的具体部分 | 主要评价指标 | 优势 | 局限与适配工作 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| **[VLN-CE-Isaac／NaVILA](https://github.com/yang-zj1026/VLN-CE-Isaac)** | **Go2 语言导航**：根据指令前进、转弯、穿过房间、到达指定位置 | 成功率 SR、路径效率 SPL、终点误差 NE | 与机器狗任务直接相关；有场景数据、预训练运动策略和评测脚本；有真机实验参考 | 依赖特定版本 Isaac Sim／Isaac Lab；Go2 策略不能直接用于 CyberDog，需要适配本体、相机和运动接口 |
+| **[VLN-PE](https://crystalsixone.github.io/vln_pe.github.io/)** | **考虑真实身体的语言导航**：四足在不同场景、光照和视角下完成路线任务 | SR、SPL、NE，以及**跌倒率、卡住率** | 能暴露普通导航仿真忽略的身体约束；适合研究导航模型到机器狗的迁移问题 | 平台和数据准备较复杂；现成四足配置不是 CyberDog；需要区分导航失败与底层运动失败 |
+| **[RobotWorld](https://github.com/robotworldai/robotworld)** | **四足任务子集**：Go2 抗推恢复、ANYmal 崎岖地形、A1 前腿倒立；另可借鉴通用 agent 评测框架 | 任务成功、交互预算、执行记录和资源消耗 | 最贴近“通用 agent 使用机器人”；动作接口和成功检查明确，适合分析失败过程 | 部分任务是关节级控制，与调用原厂走路接口差异很大；推理时暂停仿真；当前公开版本仍有复现验证缺口 |
+| **[Habitat ObjectNav](https://github.com/facebookresearch/habitat-lab)** | **自主找物**：给出“椅子／沙发”等目标类别，让机器狗搜索并接近 | SR、SPL、搜索路径与步数 | 任务定义清楚，适合比较视觉识别、探索、记忆和停止决策；可先固定运动层评测 agent | 常用配置不模拟四足步态和接触动力学；仿真成功不代表真狗能通过同一路线；迁移需处理相机高度和定位误差 |
+| **[VLN-CE：R2R／RxR](https://github.com/jacobkrantz/VLN-CE)** | **语言路线执行**：例如“出门右转，经过沙发，停在桌子旁” | SR、SPL、NE、路线符合程度 nDTW 等 | 指令、场景、评测协议较成熟；适合测语言理解、空间记忆和多步骤导航 | 对真实运动执行的简化较多；不能充分评价跌倒、打滑和身体碰撞；原仓库依赖较旧 |
+| **[Barkour](https://sites.google.com/view/barkour)** | **底层敏捷运动**：绕杆、爬坡、跳跃、上下平台 | 赛道完成时间、障碍完成情况、Barkour score | 专门面向四足运动；有明确评分规则和公开赛道资产，适合比较运动控制器 | 更偏运动控制与本体性能；若主要研究高层 agent，区分度可能有限；修改赛道后不能直接与官方成绩比较 |
+| **[MQE](https://github.com/ziyanx02/multiagent-quadruped-environment)** | **物体交互与多狗协作**：推箱、足球、过桥、合作与对抗 | 按任务统计成功、回报或胜负 | 有多种四足交互任务和预训练行走策略；适合扩展推球、推箱及多狗任务 | 主要面向多智能体强化学习；接入视觉语言 agent 需要封装观察和动作；依赖较旧的 Isaac Gym 栈 |
+
+**适合关注，但暂不作为第一项复现：**
+
+| 条目 | 对应部分 | 优势 | 当前不足 |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **[DPed-VLN](https://github.com/tju-dhj/DPedVLN)** | 动态行人环境中的语言导航、避让与安全距离 | 同时评价导航效率和社会安全，适合以后研究机器狗在人群中行动 | 本轮核查时数据已发布，评测代码仍待发布；也不是四足动力学评测 |
+| **[RCI quadruped navigation](https://github.com/RCILab/RCI_quadruped_robot_navigation)** | Go2 等机器狗的 Gazebo／Nav2 导航环境 | 可作为搭建仿真、定位和导航系统的基础 | 属于环境与工程集成；本轮查看的 README 没有完整固定任务集、评分协议和基线成绩，需自行补成 benchmark |
+
+**选型建议：**
+
+- **先跑通“语言控制机器狗”**：选 **VLN-CE-Isaac／NaVILA**。
+- **研究真实身体带来的导航失败**：选 **VLN-PE**。
+- **研究 agent 的接口使用、反馈纠错和任务完成能力**：参考 **RobotWorld** 的评测设计。
+- **研究推球、推箱或多狗协作**：参考 **MQE**。
+- **研究步态、越障、抗扰等底层控制**：选 **Barkour**。
+
+比较不同 agent 时，尽量固定机器人、传感器和底层控制器；否则最终分数很难区分是模型能力提升，还是运动系统更强。
*** End Patch"));

- **研究真实身体带来的导航失败**：选 **VLN-PE**。
- **研究 agent 的接口使用、反馈纠错和任务完成能力**：参考 **RobotWorld** 的评测设计。
- **研究推球、推箱或多狗协作**：参考 **MQE**。
- **研究步态、越障、抗扰等底层控制**：选 **Barkour**。

比较不同 agent 时，尽量固定机器人、传感器和底层控制器；否则最终分数很难区分是模型能力提升，还是运动系统更强。

264: - when researching benchmarks, the user asked for “具体的benchmark对应的部分和优劣” and then “把上面的表格塞到md里面” -> provide an actionable per-benchmark comparison and save the agreed table directly under `docs`, without reopening the completed research discussion. [Task 6]
265: - for agentic benchmarking and recent work, prioritize current arXiv/project sources and distinguish agent capability from the robot's existing low-level controller. [Task 6]
266: 
267: ## Reusable knowledge
268: - Verified environment at the time: `mi-desktop`, `aarch64`, Ubuntu 18.04.5, glibc 2.27, ROS 2 Galactic at `/opt/ros2/galactic/bin/ros2`, `ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42`, `rmw_cyclonedds_cpp`, namespace `/dog1`. Root had about 1.6 GB free while `/SDCARD` had roughly 27–28 GB; put data, Codex data, and logs on `/SDCARD`. [Task 1]
269: - Presence is not activity: check publisher count and measured frequency. `/dog1/odom_out` was about 47 Hz. `START_IMAGE_PUBLISH=9` requires nonzero width/height/FPS: `ros2 service call /dog1/camera_service protocol/srv/CameraService '{command: 9, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 5}'` produced `result=0` and `/dog1/image` about 4.99 Hz; stop with `'{command: 10}'`. [Task 1]
270: - The local YunNiao proxy at `127.0.0.1:17890` was forwarded as robot `127.0.0.1:17890`; computer, proxy, and tunnel must remain alive. Source `/SDCARD/agentic_cyberdog/codex-env.sh` in every new shell. Codex `0.163.0` was installed as `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`; its safe read-only smoke test returned `CYBERDOG_CODEX_OK`. [Task 2]
271: - CD-01A has three independent reset rounds from a fixed state, one ball push, valid contact, and displacement over an organizer-set threshold. Freeze code/version, geometry, threshold, safety/e-stop, control ownership, limits, and budgets before formal rounds; use video/markers/measurement for official judgment. [Task 3]
272: - The Go2 3.5-hour pilot stages are B0 read-only bring-up, B1 stop/timeout/client-failure tests, B2 repeatable 1 m motion and ±30° turns, B3 structured observation/action feedback, then optional A/B/C comparison. A uses raw observations plus process hints; B uses structured observations with identical hints; C uses a concise task prompt. [Task 4]
273: - SDK semantics: `SportClient.Move(vx,vy,vyaw)` is velocity/no-reply, not a distance command; `StopMove()` waits for a response; `ObstaclesAvoidClient` has no `StopMove()`; `VideoClient.GetImageSample()` returns binary image bytes. The Go2 pack has official-source labels, `robot_profile.json`, and a disabled runtime-limit template. [Task 4]
274: - Keep `observe/execute/state/stop` stable across sim and real tests, but report real adaptation separately. Keep the LLM low-frequency and local controller/watchdog/stop high-frequency; choosing among controllers is a separate experiment. [Task 4]
275: - `cyberdog67` uses `mi@10.0.0.67` / `id_ed25519`; host, aarch64, Codex login, and `codex app-server --listen stdio://` handshake were verified. Docs: `docs/cyberdog-codex-remote.md`, `docs/cyberdog-proxy.md`. [Task 5]
276: - For language-controlled quadruped navigation, start with VLN-CE-Isaac/NaVILA: Go2 tasks, SR/SPL/NE, assets, low-level policies, and evaluation scripts; adapt body, camera, and motion interfaces for CyberDog. Use VLN-PE for body-aware failure effects (collisions, falls, stuck behavior; SR/SPL/NE/TL/OS/fall/stuck metrics). [Task 6]
277: - RobotWorld is the closest conceptual reference for agentic robot-use evaluation: explicit observation/action interfaces, budgets, traces, and independent success checks. Its quadruped tasks may be joint-level and are not directly equivalent to proprietary CyberDog walking APIs; release reproducibility/validation remains a caveat. [Task 6]
278: - Use Habitat ObjectNav/VLN-CE R2R/RxR to isolate perception, search, language, memory, and planning; use Barkour (public assets/scoring) only for low-level agility; use MQE for pushbox/football/bridge/herding and multi-dog interaction, noting its MARL/older Isaac Gym basis. Do not compare modified Barkour courses to official scores. [Task 6]
279: - DPed-VLN was promising but its README said evaluation code was still being cleaned up; `RCI_quadruped_robot_navigation` is a Gazebo/Nav2 foundation, not a complete benchmark without fixed tasks, unified scoring, and baselines. Hold robot, sensors, and low-level controller fixed across agent comparisons; require video/markers or another independent real-world success check. [Task 6]
280: - Created `docs/benchmark-survey-2026-10-21.md`, bibliography/source-manifest artifacts, and `docs/benchmark-checklist-2026-10-21.md`; the latter has two tables, nine entries, task portions, metrics, advantages, limitations/adaptation work, and selection guidance. `Benchmark entries: 9` was counted. [Task 6]
281: 
282: ## Failures and how to do differently
283: - `'{command: 9}'` returned `result=1` with zero dimensions. Topic lists, service/API success, odometry, and model self-report do not prove active data or physical success -> verify live data and use an independent observation/verifier. `ros2 param dump` creates local YAML even though it does not change node parameters; label that artifact creation correctly. [Task 1]
284: - Direct SSH batch auth failed with `Permission denied (publickey,password)` when password authentication was not supplied; never retain the password. Curl saw device-code login HTTP 403, but browser authorization worked after device-code login was enabled -> do not reject the browser flow from CLI HTTP status alone. Never copy `auth.json`, API keys, VPN subscriptions, or proxy secrets. [Task 2]

Users can easily integrate the control programs developed with `Unitree_sdk2`, `unitree_ros2`, and `unitree_sdk2_python` into this simulator, enabling a seamless transition from simulation to physical development. The repository includes two versions of the simulator implemented in C++ and Python, with a structure as follows: ![](./doc/func.png) ## Directory Structure - `simulate`: Simulator implemented based on unitree_sdk2 and mujoco (C++, recommended) - `simulate_python`: Simulator implemented based on unitree_sdk2_python and mujoco (Python) - `unitree_robots`: MJCF description files for robots supported by unitree_sdk2 - `terrain_tool`: Tool for generating terrain in simulation scenarios - `example`: Example programs ## Supported Unitree sdk2 Messages: **Current version only supports low-level development, mainly used for sim to real verification of controller** - `LowCmd`: Motor control commands - `LowState`: Motor state information - `SportModeState`: Robot position and velocity data - `IMUState`: Torso IMU state at `rt/secondary_imu` topic (G1 only) Note: 1. The numbering of the motors corresponds to the actual robot hardware. Specific details can be found in the [Unitree documentation](https://support.unitree.com/home/zh/developer). 2. In the actual robot hardware, the `SportModeState` message is not readable after the built-in motion control service is turned off. However, the simulator retains this message to allow users to utilize the position and velocity information for analyzing the developed control programs. ## Related links - [unitree_sdk2](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2) - [unitree_sdk2_python](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2_python) - [unitree_ros2](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros2) - [Unitree Doc](https://support.unitree.com/home/zh/developer) - [Mujoco Doc](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/overview.html) ## Message (DDS idl) type description - Unitree Go2, B2, H1, B2w, Go2w robots use unitree_go idl for low-level communication. - Unitree G1, H1-2, and AS2 robots use unitree_hg idl for low-level communication. # Installation ## C++ Simulator (simulate) ### 1. Dependencies ```bash sudo apt install libyaml-cpp-dev libspdlog-dev libboost-all-dev libglfw3-dev ``` #### unitree_sdk2 It is recommended to install `unitree_sdk2` in `/opt/unitree_robotics` path. ```bash git clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2.git cd unitree_sdk2/ mkdir build cd build cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/unitree_robotics sudo make install ``` For more details, see: https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2 #### mujoco Download the mujoco [release](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/releases), and extract it to the `~/.mujoco` directory; ``` cd unitree_mujoco/simulate/ ln -s ~/.mujoco/mujoco-3.3.6 mujoco ``` ### 2. Compile unitree_mujoco ```bash cd unitree_mujoco/simulate mkdir build && cd build cmake .. make -j4 ``` ### 3. Test: Run: ```bash ./unitree_mujoco -r go2 -s scene_terrain.xml ``` You should see the mujoco simulator with the Go2 robot loaded. In a new terminal, run: ```bash ./test ``` The program will output the robot's pose and position information in the simulator, and each motor of the robot will continuously output 1Nm of torque. **Note:** The testing program sends the unitree_go message. If you want to test G1 robot, you need to modify the program to use the unitree_hg message. ### AS2 simulation AS2 uses the `unitree_hg` low-level messages. The simulator selects that IDL automatically when `-r as2` is used; `-t 1` can be supplied to make the choice explicit. From `simulate/build`, start the flat scene with: ```bash ./unitree_mujoco -r as2 -s plane_terrain.xml -t 1 ``` Use `scene_terrain.xml` instead for the rough-terrain scene. ## Python Simulator (simulate_python) ### 1. Dependencies #### unitree_sdk2_python ```bash cd ~ sudo apt install python3-pip git clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2_python.git cd unitree_sdk2_python pip3 install -e . ``` If you encounter an error during installation: ```bash Could not locate cyclonedds. Try to set CYCLONEDDS_HOME or CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH ``` Refer to: https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2_python #### mujoco-python ```bash pip3 install mujoco ``` #### joystick ```bash pip3 install pygame ``` ### 2. Test ```bash cd ./simulate_python python3 ./unitree_mujoco.py ``` You should see the mujoco simulator with the Go2 robot loaded. In a new terminal, run: ```bash python3 ./test/test_unitree_sdk2.py ``` The program will output the robot's pose and position information in the simulator, and each motor of the robot will continuously output 1Nm of torque. **Note:** The testing program sends the unitree_go message. If you want to test G1 robot, you need to modify the program to use the unitree_hg message. # Usage ## 1. Simulation Configuration ### C++ Simulator The configuration file for the C++ simulator is located at `/simulate/config.yaml`: ```yaml # Robot name loaded by the simulator # "go2", "b2", "b2w", "h1", "go2w", "g1", "h2", "as2" robot: "go2" # Robot simulation scene file # For example, for go2, it refers to the scene.xml file in the /unitree_robots/go2/ folder robot_scene: "scene.xml" # DDS domain id, it is recommended to distinguish from the real robot (default is 0 on the real robot) domain_id: 1 # -1: automatic, 0: unitree_go, 1: unitree_hg # Automatic mode selects unitree_hg for as2. idl_type: -1 use_joystick: 1 # Simulate Unitree WirelessController using a gamepad joystick_type: "xbox" # support "xbox" and "switch" gamepad layout joystick_device: "/dev/input/js0" # Device path joystick_bits: 16 # Some game controllers may only have 8-bit accuracy # Network interface name, for simulation, it is recommended to use the local loopback "lo" interface: "lo" # Whether to output robot link, joint, sensor information, 1 for output print_scene_information: 1 # Whether to use virtual tape, 1 to enable # Mainly used to simulate the hanging process of H1 robot initialization enable_elastic_band: 0 # For H1 ``` ### Python Simulator The configuration file for the Python simulator is located at `/simulate_python/config.py`: ```python # Robot name loaded by the simulator # "go2", "b2", "b2w", "h1" ROBOT = "go2" # Robot simulation scene file ROBOT_SCENE = "../unitree_robots/" + ROBOT + "/scene.xml" # Robot scene # DDS domain id, it is recommended to distinguish from the real robot (default is 0 on the real robot) DOMAIN_ID = 1 # Domain id # Network interface name, for simulation, it is recommended to use the local loopback "lo" INTERFACE = "lo" # Interface # Whether to output robot link, joint, sensor information, True for output PRINT_SCENE_INFORMATION = True USE_JOYSTICK = 1 # Simulate Unitree WirelessController using a gamepad JOYSTICK_TYPE = "xbox" # support "xbox" and "switch" gamepad layout JOYSTICK_DEVICE = 0 # Joystick number # Whether to use virtual tape, 1 to enable # Mainly used to simulate the hanging process of H1 robot initialization ENABLE_ELASTIC_BAND = False # Simulation time step (unit: s) # To ensure the reliability of the simulation, it needs to be greater than the time required for viewer.sync() to render once SIMULATE_DT = 0.003 # Visualization interface runtime step, 0.02 corresponds to 50fps/s VIEWER_DT = 0.02 ``` ### Joystick The simulator will use an Xbox or Switch gamepad to simulate the wireless controller of the robot. The button and joystick information of the wireless controller will be published through "rt/wireless_controller" topic. `use_joystick/USE_JOYSTICK` in `config.yaml/config.py` needs to be set to 0, when there is no gamepad. If your gamepad is not in Xbox or Switch layout, you can modify it in the source code (The button and joystick IDs can be determined using `jstest`): In `simulate/src/unitree_sdk2_bridge/unitree_sdk2_bridge.cc`: ```C++ if (js_type == "xbox") { js_id_.axis["LX"] = 0; // Left stick axis x js_id_.axis["LY"] = 1; // Left stick axis y js_id_.axis["RX"] = 3; // Right stick axis x js_id_.axis["RY"] = 4; // Right stick axis y js_id_.axis["LT"] = 2; // Left trigger js_id_.axis["RT"] = 5; // Right trigger js_id_.axis["DX"] = 6; // Directional pad x js_id_.axis["DY"] = 7; // Directional pad y js_id_.button["X"] = 2; js_id_.button["Y"] = 3; js_id_.button["B"] = 1; js_id_.button["A"] = 0; js_id_.button["LB"] = 4; js_id_.button["RB"] = 5; js_id_.button["SELECT"] = 6; js_id_.button["START"] = 7; } ``` In `simulate_python/unitree_sdk2_bridge.py`: ```python if js_type == "xbox": self.axis_id = { "LX": 0, # Left stick axis x "LY": 1, # Left stick axis y "RX": 3, # Right stick axis x "RY": 4, # Right stick axis y "LT": 2, # Left trigger "RT": 5, # Right trigger "DX": 6, # Directional pad x "DY": 7, # Directional pad y } self.button_id = { "X": 2, "Y": 3, "B": 1, "A": 0, "LB": 4, "RB": 5, "SELECT": 6, "START": 7, } ``` ### Elastic band for humanoid Consider humanoid robots are not suitable for starting in ground, a virtual elastic band was designed to simulate the lifting and lowering of humanoid robots. Setting ` enable_elastic_mand/ENABLE_ELSTIC_BAND=1 ` can enable the virtual elastic band. After loading the robot, press' 9 'to activate or release the strap, press' 7' to lower the robot, and press' 8 'to lift the robot. ## 2. Terrain Generation Tool We provide a tool to parametrically create simple terrains in the mujoco simulator, including stairs, rough ground, and height maps. The program is located in the `terrain_tool` folder. For specific usage instructions, refer to the README file in the `terrain_tool` folder. ![Terrain Generation Example](./doc/terrain.png) ## 3. Sim to Real The `example` folder contains simple examples of using different interfaces to make the Go2 robot stand up and then lie down. These examples demonstrate how to implement the transition from simulation to reality using interfaces provided by Unitree. Here is an explanation of each folder name: - `cpp`: Based on C++, using `unitree_sdk2` interface - `python`: Based on Python, using `unitree_sdk2_python` interface - `ros2`: Based on ROS2, using `unitree_ros2` interface ### unitree_sdk2 1. Run: ```bash ./stand_go2 # Control the robot in the simulation (make sure the Go2 simulation scene has been loaded) ./stand_go2 enp3s0 # Control the physical robot, where enp3s0 is the name of the network card connected to the robot ``` 3. unitreerobotics__unitree_rl_lab # Unitree RL Lab [![IsaacSim](https://img.shields.io/badge/IsaacSim-5.1.0-silver.svg)](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/isaacsim/latest/overview.html) [![Isaac Lab](https://img.shields.io/badge/IsaacLab-2.3.0-silver)](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache2.0-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Discord-5865F2?style=flat&logo=Discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/ZwcVwxv5rq) ## Overview This project provides a set of reinforcement learning environments for Unitree robots, built on top of [IsaacLab](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab). Currently supports Unitree **Go2**, **H1** and **G1-29dof** robots.

## Installation - Install Isaac Lab by following the [installation guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/main/source/setup/installation/index.html). - Install the Unitree RL IsaacLab standalone environments. - Clone or copy this repository separately from the Isaac Lab installation (i.e. outside the `IsaacLab` directory): ```bash git clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_lab.git ``` - Use a python interpreter that has Isaac Lab installed, install the library in editable mode using: ```bash conda activate env_isaaclab ./unitree_rl_lab.sh -i # restart your shell to activate the environment changes. ``` - Download unitree robot description files *Method 1: Using USD Files* - Download unitree usd files from [unitree_model](https://huggingface.co/datasets/unitreerobotics/unitree_model/tree/main), keeping folder structure ```bash git clone https://huggingface.co/datasets/unitreerobotics/unitree_model ``` - Config `UNITREE_MODEL_DIR` in `source/unitree_rl_lab/unitree_rl_lab/assets/robots/unitree.py`. ```bash UNITREE_MODEL_DIR = "" ``` *Method 2: Using URDF Files [Recommended]* Only for Isaacsim >= 5.0 - Download unitree robot urdf files from [unitree_ros](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros) ``` git clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros.git ``` - Config `UNITREE_ROS_DIR` in `source/unitree_rl_lab/unitree_rl_lab/assets/robots/unitree.py`. ```bash UNITREE_ROS_DIR = "" ``` - [Optional]: change *robot_cfg.spawn* if you want to use urdf files - Verify that the environments are correctly installed by: - Listing the available tasks: ```bash ./unitree_rl_lab.sh -l # This is a faster version than isaaclab ``` - Running a task: ```bash ./unitree_rl_lab.sh -t --task Unitree-G1-29dof-Velocity # support for autocomplete task-name # same as python scripts/rsl_rl/train.py --headless --task Unitree-G1-29dof-Velocity ``` - Inference with a trained agent: ```bash ./unitree_rl_lab.sh -p --task Unitree-G1-29dof-Velocity # support for autocomplete task-name # same as python scripts/rsl_rl/play.py --task Unitree-G1-29dof-Velocity ``` ## Deploy After the model training is completed, we need to perform sim2sim on the trained strategy in Mujoco to test the performance of the model. Then deploy sim2real. ### Setup ```bash # Install dependencies sudo apt install -y libyaml-cpp-dev libboost-all-dev libeigen3-dev libspdlog-dev libfmt-dev # Install unitree_sdk2 git clone git@github.com:unitreerobotics/unitree_sdk2.git cd unitree_sdk2 mkdir build && cd build cmake .. -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF # Install on the /usr/local directory sudo make install # Compile the robot_controller cd unitree_rl_lab/deploy/robots/g1_29dof # or other robots mkdir build && cd build cmake .. && make ``` ### Sim2Sim Installing the [unitree_mujoco](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco?tab=readme-ov-file#installation). - Set the `robot` at `/simulate/config.yaml` to g1 - Set `domain_id` to 0 - Set `enable_elastic_hand` to 1 - Set `use_joystck` to 1. ```bash # start simulation cd unitree_mujoco/simulate/build ./unitree_mujoco # ./unitree_mujoco -i 0 -n eth0 -r g1 -s scene_29dof.xml # alternative ``` ```bash cd unitree_rl_lab/deploy/robots/g1_29dof/build ./g1_ctrl # 1. press [L2 + Up] to set the robot to stand up # 2. Click the mujoco window, and then press 8 to make the robot feet touch the ground. # 3. Press [R1 + X] to run the policy. # 4. Click the mujoco window, and then press 9 to disable the elastic band. ``` ### Sim2Real You can use this program to control the robot directly, but make sure the on-borad control program has been closed. ```bash ./g1_ctrl --network eth0 # eth0 is the network interface name. ``` ## Acknowledgements This repository is built upon the support and contributions of the following open-source projects. *** Add File: D:/Project/AgenticCyberDog/docs/go2-simulation-environments-2026-10-24.md
+# Unitree Go2 官方与社区仿真环境核查
+
+核查日期：2026-10-24。证据来自官方 GitHub 仓库、当前源码、维护者支持表和发布记录。本次没有安装仿真器、运行控制策略或连接机器人；下文区分“官方支持”“维护者报告验证”和“本机实测”，不把前两者表述为本机跑通。
+
+**结论：Go2 有官方仿真环境，也有公开控制器和维护者真机验证记录的社区方案。** 官方优先考察 `unitree_mujoco` 和 `unitree_rl_lab`；如果想尽快获得能行走并接受高层速度指令的仿真 Go2，可优先考察 `rl_sar`。
+
+最重要的边界是：**Go2 模型、关节级 SDK 仿真、可行走的控制策略、原厂高层运动服务是四件不同的事。** 不能因为模型能加载或有 `SportModeState` 状态消息，就认为真机的 `SportClient.Move()`、避障、相机取流等服务已被完整仿真。
+
+| 方案 | 来源与 Go2 支持证据 | 可以直接利用的部分 | 优势 | 局限及适用判断 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| **[unitree_mujoco](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco)** | 宇树官方；有 Go2 MJCF、场景和 C++ / Python / ROS 2 站立示例 | MuJoCo 物理仿真；SDK2 / DDS 的 `LowCmd`、`LowState`、`SportModeState`；简单地形生成工具 | 官方协议适配明确；适合关节控制、控制器调试和 sim-to-real 接口准备；相对完整 Isaac 场景栈更轻 | README 明确说当前主要支持低层开发。默认示例不是完整行走控制器，不能直接视作原厂 SportClient 服务替身；视觉导航的传感器和任务层需另补 |
+| **[unitree_rl_lab](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_lab)** | 宇树官方；明确支持 Go2；源码注册 `Unitree-Go2-Velocity`，有 `deploy/robots/go2/` | Isaac Lab 中的 Go2 速度跟踪训练、回放、控制器部署；配合官方 MuJoCo 做 sim-to-sim | 官方训练与部署路线；训练和机器人动作接口比仅有模型更完整；适合研究步态和底层策略 | 需要 Isaac 环境及模型资产；Go2 部署配置默认指向自己的训练日志目录，本轮未找到仓库自带 Go2 策略权重或 release 权重包。README 的主要部署演示是 G1，不能拿它代替 Go2 实测证据 |
+| **[Isaac Lab](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab)** | NVIDIA / Isaac Lab 官方框架，非宇树维护；当前源码明确注册 Go2 平地和粗糙地形速度跟踪环境 | 标准化 RL 环境、地形、奖励、训练算法配置和传感器扩展 | 通用机器人学习生态较完整；适合并行训练、系统性控制实验和后续扩展 | 不是 Go2 原厂固件仿真；训练任务不自动等于语言导航任务。不同版本的路径、任务名和接口会变化，要与上层项目固定匹配 |
+| **[rl_sar](https://github.com/fan-ziqi/rl_sar)** | 社区项目；维护者支持表明确标注 Go2 在 Gazebo / MuJoCo / 真机可用；有 Go2 配置、策略文件和实机控制代码 | 预训练行走策略、C++ 仿真和部署程序；Gazebo 的 ROS 1 / ROS 2 路径具有 `/cmd_vel` 订阅及导航模式 | **较适合快速做能走的 agent 原型。** 仓库中有 `policy/go2/himloco/himloco.pt` 和 `policy/go2/robot_lab/policy.pt`，不只给空模型；有版本发布和 Docker 支持 | 非宇树官方；“真机可用”是维护者报告，本次未独立复现。它使用自己的运动策略，不能假设与原厂控制器响应相同；Python 版暂停维护，优先按当前 C++ 路线使用；Gazebo 路径依赖 Classic |
+| **[VLN-CE-Isaac / NaVILA](https://github.com/yang-zj1026/VLN-CE-Isaac)** | 研究团队公开平台；Go2 导航环境、低层策略、数据入口和评测脚本明确 | 语言指令导航，室内场景，SR / SPL / NE 等指标 | 对当前 agent benchmark 项目最直接；同时具备物理本体和任务集 | 仓库固定 Isaac Sim 4.1.0 / 修改版 Isaac Lab 1.1.0；文档明确提示新版本兼容性未知；它是特定研究协议，不是通用官方 Go2 SDK 模拟器 |
+
+**官方 MuJoCo 的证据最明确，但需补行走控制器。**
+
+官方 README 原文：
+
+> Current version only supports low-level development, mainly used for sim to real verification of controller.
+
+其 C++ 文档提供了 `./unitree_mujoco -r go2 -s scene_terrain.xml` 启动示例，仓库还有 `example/python/stand_go2.py`、`example/cpp/stand_go2.cpp` 和 ROS 2 示例。这里的站立/趴下演示证明了低层接口使用方式；并不等于已经提供完整的导航、行走、避障服务。
+
+源码和文档入口：
+
+- [Go2 模型与场景](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco/tree/main/unitree_robots/go2)
+- [Go2 Python 低层示例](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco/blob/main/example/python/stand_go2.py)
+- [官方 RL Lab 的 Go2 训练任务](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_lab/tree/main/source/unitree_rl_lab/unitree_rl_lab/tasks/locomotion/robots/go2)
+- [官方 RL Lab 的 Go2 部署目录](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_lab/tree/main/deploy/robots/go2)
+- [Go2 部署配置：策略目录指向训练日志](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_lab/blob/main/deploy/robots/go2/config/config.yaml)
+
+**几个容易混淆的项目与版本问题：**
+
+| 项目 / 问题 | 本轮查到的事实 | 判断 |
+|---|---|---|
+| [unitree_sim_isaaclab](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_sim_isaaclab) | 是宇树官方，但 README 当前明确介绍的是 G1 / H1-2 任务；本轮目录检索未找到 Go2 专用实现 | 不应因为名称含 Unitree 和 Isaac Lab 就将其列为已支持 Go2 的首选环境；Go2 优先查 `unitree_rl_lab` |
+| [unitree_rl_gym](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym) | 官方旧 Isaac Gym 路线，确实有 Go2 训练配置；但当前 `deploy/pre_train/` 和 `deploy/deploy_mujoco/configs/` 查到的是 G1/H1/H1_2，未查到 Go2 对应文件 | 可以研究/复用训练，但不能声称当前仓库已提供 Go2 的整套预训练 sim-to-sim 部署包；新训练项目优先考察 RL Lab |
+| [unitree_ros](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros) | 官方 Go2 URDF 和 Gazebo 文件存在；README 明确提示 Gazebo 仿真提供低层关节控制，不包含高层走路控制 | 官方机器人模型与低层仿真基础，不是开箱即用的自主导航系统 |
+| [MuJoCo Menagerie Go2](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie/tree/main/unitree_go2) | Google DeepMind 维护的模型集合；Go2 MJCF 从宇树公开 URDF 派生，包含简化接触模型 | 可作为可信来源明确的模型资产，不应称作“宇树官方完整控制环境”或“原厂行为等价数字孪生” |
+| Isaac Lab 版本匹配 | 查到 [Isaac Lab 3.0.0](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/releases/tag/v3.0.0) 于 2026-10-20 发布；但 Unitree RL Lab README 仍标注 Isaac Sim 5.1.0 / Isaac Lab 2.3.0 | 不把“最新 Isaac Lab”直接与旧项目拼接；复现宇树项目先按其声明的版本配置，新版本兼容性另外验证 |
+| Gazebo Classic | [官方页面](https://classic.gazebosim.org/)标明已于 2025-01 结束生命周期；rl_sar 的 Gazebo 路线使用 Classic | 现有项目仍可复用，但长期新平台要考虑维护成本；不能把 Classic 和新版 Gazebo 当成可直接替换的依赖 |
+
+**对 Agent4CyberDog / Go2 项目的选型建议：**
+
+1. **想最快做 agent 调用速度指令、控制一只会走的虚拟 Go2：优先考察 `rl_sar`。** 使用固定预训练运动策略，把 agent 的前进、转向、停止等工具接到控制层。已核实的 `/cmd_vel` 接口属于其 ROS / Gazebo 路线；若选 MuJoCo 路线，需单独确认或补上 agent 到控制器的适配，不假设两者接口相同。
+2. **想保留宇树 SDK2 的低层通信结构：选择 `unitree_mujoco`，另外配一个经过验证的 Go2 控制器。** 官方 `unitree_rl_lab` 有 Go2 训练/部署代码，但仍需准备相应训练结果，不能直接假设已提供现成权重。
+3. **想训练或改进步态、地形通过能力：选择 `unitree_rl_lab` 或 Isaac Lab 的 Go2 任务。** 这是控制策略研发路线，工作量高于直接使用已有步态。
+4. **想马上做语言导航 benchmark：继续使用 NaVILA / VLN-CE-Isaac 这类已有任务集的平台。** 通用模拟器解决物理和接口，benchmark 还要额外提供固定任务、成功检查及统计协议。
+
